The simulation strategy is better. I have use it too as it allowed to compute other things. Then consider p + (1-p)m, where p and m are the mean of each one, the probability of positives and positive part.

On Thu, Jul 19, 2018, 17:12 Ruby Ji <crysta...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all, 

I am trying to make predictions from a hurdle model. I got the predictions of occurrence probability and positive values using: 

zpre <-res$summary.fitted.values[inla.stack.index(stk,"pred.z")$data, "mean"]
ypre <-res$summary.fitted.values[inla.stack.index(stk,"pred.y")$data, "mean"]

Then I got the predictions by multiplying the above two.

1. Is it correct?
2. May I get 1000 predictions for each site? The summary.fitted.values only provides mean and sd.

Thanks,
Ruby
